note: Version history of the calculation rulesets, jurisdiction rule packs and calendar data. Each entry lists what changed and the sources behind it. Commit hashes refer to the GitHub repository.

entries.title: Singapore Side-by-Side exemption for US-parented groups; legislative status basis
changes: New group input 'Ultimate parent is a US entity (US-parented group, Side-by-Side)'. It is off by default and saved with the group and with scenarios.

When the group is US-parented and an SG parent would apply the IIR for an FY commencing on or after 1 Jan 2026, Singapore's MTT (IIR) is not charged. Trail: 'SG IIR exempt under the Side-by-Side package (passed, not yet law)', linked to the source. A non-SG intermediate parent with an IIR in force takes over if there is one; otherwise the residual top-up is shown as 'SbS exempt' and excluded from the total top-up. Singapore's DTT is unchanged.

The 'TCSH basis' setting is renamed 'legislative status basis' (the stored field is still tcshBasis). Enacted law only (default): the SG IIR is still charged, with a note that it would be exempt once enacted. Enacted + passed / announced, or OECD terms: the exemption applies.

Dashboard: amber 'Not yet law' risk line ('Relies on passed-not-yet-enacted law') whenever the exemption is relied on; RAG amber for a jurisdiction whose top-up is exempt only for this reason. Results page callout, CSV column and Jurisdictions page block added.

Not modelled: Japan's Side-by-Side IIR exemption (the JP pack sources it: FY2026 reform outline, plus the US designation reported via a secondary source) and any Hong Kong equivalent (none sourced). The UTPR side of the SbS Safe Harbour elsewhere is not modelled either.
OECD parameters unchanged (globe-params.v0.5.json).

entries.title: Singapore: Finance (Income Taxes) Bill 2026 passed; Side-by-Side Safe Harbour block
changes: Bill No. 22/2026 recorded as passed by Parliament on 6 Oct 2026, with presidential assent and gazetting pending (MOF speech; CNA confirms passage).

New sideBySideSafeHarbour block: legal status 'passed-not-enacted', applies to the MTT (IIR) only, effective 'for financial years commencing on or after 1 January 2026' (IRAS; Bill s.1(4), cl.38(2) and new s.84(3)). Qualifying groups are set by regulations that refer to the OECD list of qualified side-by-side regimes; MOF names US MNEs. The DTT is unaffected.
Safe-harbour status text, TCSH extension note and the 'Pending amendments' feature updated; MOF and CNA added to the sources.

entries.title: Local adoption of the Transitional CbCR Safe Harbour
changes: The TCSH transition period now follows the collecting jurisdiction's law, read from its rule pack: the domestic top-up tax law first, then the IIR parent's law, otherwise OECD terms.
New input 'TCSH basis': enacted law (default), enacted plus officially announced, or OECD terms everywhere.
Assumptions are flagged where local law is silent (HKMTT).
OECD parameters unchanged from v0.3 (globe-params.v0.4.json).

entries.title: Hong Kong: TCSH adoption block
changes: The TCSH applies to the IIR under Sch. 61 Pt 3 Div. 2 IRO, for FYs beginning on or before 31 Dec 2026 and ending on or before 30 Jun 2028 (verified).
Whether the TCSH also zeroes HKMTT is not expressly stated (unverified; the engine assumes yes and flags it).
The OECD 2027 extension is not adopted: no s.26AG notice or IRD announcement found (unverified absence).

entries.title: Singapore: TCSH adoption block
changes: The TCSH applies to both MTT (IIR) and DTT for FYs beginning on or before 31 Dec 2026 and ending on or before 30 Jun 2028 (IRAS Module 6, June 2026; verified).
Extension to FYs beginning on or before 31 Dec 2027 announced by IRAS (amendments by end-2026, subject to Parliament); not yet enacted.

entries.title: Japan: TCSH adoption block
changes: TCSH for the IIR and the QDMTT; the one-year extension (FYs beginning by end-2027) was enacted by Act No. 12 of 31 Mar 2026, in force 1 Apr 2026 (verified).
The end limb (30 Jun 2029) follows the OECD SbS Package and is not quoted from Japanese law.

entries.title: Deadline roll-forward and 2026–2027 public holidays
changes: Filing calendar shows the statutory and the adjusted due date.
HK (Cap. 1 s.71: general holidays incl. Sundays), SG (Interpretation Act s.50: Sundays and public holidays), JP (National Tax General Act Art. 10(2): Sat/Sun, holidays, 29 Dec–3 Jan).
Holiday lists for 2026–2027 only, from GovHK / 1823, MOM and the Cabinet Office. Other years use the weekend rule only and are flagged.
ICS (calendar) export added.

entries.title: Entity-level GloBE engine
changes: Entities blended by jurisdiction, with SBIE on payroll and tangible assets at the Art. 9.2 transition rates.
TCSH tests (de minimis, simplified ETR 15/15/16/17/17%, routine profits) on CbCR inputs, over the OECD transition period as extended by the SbS Package.
Ordering: QDMTT (with QDMTT Safe Harbour status), then the IIR at the parent × ownership %, then a flagged UTPR residual.
Simplified Art. 4.4.1 deferred tax recast at 15%.
